newsDocuments.headline: Yemen's Houthis vow more attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities after Aramco HQ hit

segments.text: RIYADH/DUBAI: Yemen’s Houthis vowed on Wednesday to press on with attacks on airports and oil facilities in Saudi Arabia, a day after a strike that sources said caused extensive damage to the headquarters of oil giant Saudi Aramco.

Tuesday night’s attack on Saudi Aramco’s base in the eastern city of Dhahran caused a fire that spread across several floors, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters . The Saudi energy ministry had said the strike caused a li
The escalating conflict has dealt a blow to Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s ambitious plans to transform and diversify the Saudi economy and reduce its reliance on oil.

newsDocuments.headline: Diesel deal opens way for more Russia-US cooperation, Kremlin envoy says

segments.text: MOSCOW: A Russia-US deal on supplies of Russian diesel can pave the way for further economic cooperation between the two countries, Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev said on Wednesday, adding that Moscow would overcome any sanctions-related dif
US President Donald Trump said last Friday that he and Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin had reached an agreement for Russia to release supplies of diesel to the US and global markets.
Trump is keen to lower US diesel prices ahead of November 3 US mid-term elections.

newsDocuments.headline: Palm oil gains for third session, tracking crude and Dalian

segments.text: JAKARTA: Malaysian palm oil futures closed higher for a third straight session on Wednesday, buoyed by stronger crude oil prices and gains in rival edible oils on the Dalian market.
The benchmark palm oil contract for December delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 17 ringgit, or 0.36%, to 4,699 ringgit ($1,151.72) a metric ton at the close.
“The FCPO is tracking Dalian performance and crude oil prices today,” a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

newsDocuments.headline: Indian shares end lower as higher oil prices, foreign outflows dent appetite

segments.text: Indian shares closed lower on Wednesday as firmer oil prices and sustained foreign outflows weighed on risk sentiment after a rebound in the previous session, while investors assessed earnings and awaited key US inflation data.
Oil prices rose to $106a barrel after two vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz, heightening supply concerns, while Iranian officials said they were deploying new tactics to target ships.
